finding: Path.resolve() returns the stored letter case only on Windows; on a case-insensitive POSIX file system (default macOS, which bootstrap.sh supports) two spellings of one description file still get two work ids, so a re-run files a second ticket
why: D-34 rests on 'the resolved path carries the stored spelling', but posixpath.realpath only follows symlinks and keeps each part exactly as typed, so the round-4 case-insensitivity fix holds on Windows alone and the new test fails on macOS instead of skipping (`other.exists()` is True there).
fix: Take the stored names from the directory itself, e.g. pick the os.scandir(parent) entry for which os.path.samefile(entry, source) is true (same for the folder), rather than relying on resolve() to normalise case.
evidence: publish_bug_mode.py:381-383 `real = source.resolve()` / `hashlib.sha1(f"{real.parent.name}/{real.name}"...` ; stdlib posixpath.realpath (afk-python 3.14.8) docstring 'eliminating any symbolic links encountered in the path' and its loop sets `path = newpath` (the typed name) for every non-link part; on Windows the check `Path('.../case/export/description.md').resolve()` printed `...\case\Export\DESCRIPTION.md` (case normalised), which no POSIX code path does; macOS supported: CHANGELOG.md:313 'bootstrap.sh (macOS, Linux)', MANIFEST.md:970 'folded on Windows and macOS'. Not run on macOS (no macOS host; CI matrix is ubuntu-latest + windows-latest) — inferred from the stdlib source.

finding: One test checks two behaviours and a mid-body `if ... pytest.skip` decides whether the second (the only half that guards the delta) runs
why: The first half (same path re-run) passed before this delta too, so on a case-sensitive file system the test reports `skipped` after asserting nothing the delta changed, and a reader cannot tell from the name which half guards D-34.
fix: Split into a plain same-path re-run test and a case-variant test whose case-sensitivity check sits in a `skipif`/fixture before any assertion.
evidence: test_publish_bug_mode.py:948-962 `def test_a_re_run_of_one_description_file_keeps_its_work_id` ... `assert sorted(stub.issues) == ["1"] and stub.comments("1") == []` then `if not other.exists():` / `pytest.skip("the file system tells letter case apart")` then a second identical assert block; mutants M2/M3 (pre-delta work id spelling) are killed only by the post-skip half.
